title: Specialization datum and specialization of a correspondence
statement:
Use the finite coefficient and scheme conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, $k$ algebraically closed and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Set $R=k[t]_{(t)}$, $D=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with closed point $0$, generic point $\eta$ and a chosen geometric generic point $\bar\eta$. A lift of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ is a separated finite-type $D$-scheme $\widetilde T$ with $\rho:\widetilde T\to T\times_kD$ whose generic fibre is an isomorphism. Write $T_0=\widetilde T\times_D0$. For an etale complex $M$, define
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}M=R\Psi_{\widetilde T}(\rho_\eta^*M_\eta).$$
Here $R\Psi$ means $i^*Rj_*M_{\bar\eta}$ after passage to the strict henselization of $D$, where $j:\widetilde T_{\bar\eta}\to\widetilde T_{D^{\rm sh}}$ and $i:T_0\to\widetilde T_{D^{\rm sh}}$ are the natural maps. The project pro-etale version is the pullback by the etale/pro-etale comparison of this construction on the etale representative; [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] specifies that representative on bounded constructible objects. Write $\omega_T=Ra_T^!A$ as in [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. The specialization map on Borel--Moore sections is the map
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}:\operatorname{Hom}(A_T,\omega_T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(A_{T_0},\omega_{T_0})$$
obtained by specializing sections and applying the nearby-cycle unit on $A$ and the exceptional base-change map on $\omega$.

If a correspondence $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_kX$ of [def-trf-correspondence] has a lift $\widetilde c:\widetilde C\to\widetilde X\times_D\widetilde X$, write $b=(b_1,b_2)=\widetilde c_0$. For the exceptional adjoint $\widehat u:Rc_{1!}c_2^*K\to K$ of $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$, define its specialized coefficient morphism by the exceptional adjoint of
$$Rb_{1!}b_2^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}K\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}^*}Rb_{1!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde C}c_2^*K\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}_!}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}Rc_{1!}c_2^*K\xrightarrow{\operatorname{sp}(\widehat u)}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}K.$$
The base-change maps here are those induced from the usual ordinary and exceptional adjunctions through the displayed nearby-cycle construction. This defines $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde c}u:b_2^*\operatorname{sp}K\to b_1^!\operatorname{sp}K$.
